findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 4
Raise: Security
The rule says, "Input is checked where it enters." A pull request author can edit the shared record so `summary.folded` has valid `start` and `end` timestamps but a string `working` value. `from_body()` accepts it because its validation calls `merged()` without checking folded category values. When `forge board` builds the story, this `min()` compares the string with seconds and raises `TypeError`, making the board unavailable.
findings.title: Standard: Input is checked where it enters

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
`_claim()` assigns folded working seconds to the earliest still-unknown interval, regardless of when that work occurred. If one task's folded ten-minute range contains five minutes of work followed by five minutes of waiting, while another task has recorded work during the first five minutes, the story already marks that first half as working. This code assigns the folded work to the second half and drops its waiting time, showing ten minutes working instead of five working and five waiting. The new overlapping-parts proof checks only a category upper bound, so it passes with this breakdown.
findings.title: Story breakdown miscounts overlapping folded task time

why: A long item's pull request time record grows toward GitHub's 64 KB body limit, and Forge trims older time detail from about round 16
